name: Iron Pike
summary: In Lakeshire, Iron Pike supplies are needed to repair the Everstill Bridge. The shipment from Stormwind was seized by Redridge gnolls, leaving the town short of iron.

sections.title: Stolen Caravan Cargo
sections.body: Lakeshire spent its metal reserves forging armor, blades, and ammunition after recent attacks by the Blackrock orcs. Builders requested more iron from Stormwind City, but Redridge gnolls hijacked the caravan on the road. They carried crates of iron pikes and rivets north into the hills, stopping repairs on the Everstill Bridge.

sections.title: Rebuilding the Span
sections.body: Foreman Oslow oversees the bridge's reconstruction and needs the stolen hardware back. Without the heavy pikes to reinforce its stone and timber frame, the bridge leaves Lakeshire partly cut off from the northern road and open to further incursions.

faq.q: Why are the gnolls carrying construction pikes?
aliases: why do gnolls have iron pikes
where did gnolls get iron pikes
faq.answer: The gnolls ambushed a supply caravan traveling from Stormwind to Lakeshire, then scattered into the Redridge hills with crates of stolen construction supplies, including iron pikes and rivets.

faq.q: Who needs these iron pikes in Lakeshire?
faq.answer: Foreman Oslow needs the pikes to rebuild the Everstill Bridge across Lake Everstill. Lakeshire has no spare iron after melting its reserves into weapons and armor during recent orc attacks.

faq.q: Where can these iron pikes be recovered?
faq.answer: Redridge gnolls hold the pikes in their camps in the hills and ridges north of Lakeshire.

faq.q: Why couldn't Lakeshire just forge their own iron pikes?
faq.answer: Lakeshire used its local iron supply fighting the Blackrock orcs, melting the metal into swords, bullets, and protective gear. The town had to ask Stormwind for new iron for construction.

angles.text: As an Alliance traveler, recovering the stolen supplies helps secure Lakeshire's crossings and fortify Stormwind's eastern border against Blackrock aggression.
As a blacksmith, you can see how war strained local smiths: all their raw iron had to go toward weapons.
